metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated system menu → Settings → Power panel in 5 turns. Correctly identified no battery present and declared [INFEASIBLE]. Evaluator rewarded 1.0.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can click system tray menu, open Settings app, navigate to Power panel, scroll through settings panels.
metadata.explanation: Agent proved ability to open GNOME Settings and navigate panels. This task exercises the same Settings navigation while requiring a concrete, verifiable change: enabling seconds in the clock. Evaluator checks 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-show-seconds' equals 'true'. Initial state is 'false' (screenshot shows 19:33 without seconds), so negative-control resistance is satisfied.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-show-seconds', which is the authoritative GNOME setting for showing seconds in the top-panel clock.

Metric 'check_include_exclude' receives the rules dict directly (via get_rule returning config['rules']), and correctly accesses rules.get('include') and rules.get('exclude') — no parameter-handling error.
Expected values are semantically correct: include=['true'] and exclude=['false'] match the exact string output of the gsettings command when seconds are enabled.
No postconfig required: gsettings reads from the settings database directly, not from a transient UI dialog.
Negative-control resistance is satisfied: the initial state is 'false' (clock displays without seconds), so a do-nothing agent would fail evaluation.
Instruction has a single requirement (enable seconds display) and the evaluator checks exactly that requirement — full coverage.
